# B"H
<!-- Boruch Hashem -->
<!-- Blessed is He -->

# Remaining Work Ledger

> From Awtsmoos the hidden path is shown,
> through Awtsmoos.com each broken route is known.

## Mission

Restore `/games/mitzvahWorld/` so its source-mode and CompactJS-generated runtime both boot, load required assets, resolve dynamic modules, and expose working movement, combat, inventory, quest, recovery, and streaming readiness.

## Observed Evidence

- Browser console reports `MINIMAL_MEADOW_NOT_PLAYABLE: inventory,equipment,combat,quest,recovery,streaming`.
- Chossid model hydration requests a malformed path containing `/assets/models/player/d86fd32.../chossid.glb` and receives HTTP 404.
- Optional chat imports resolve beneath an incorrect `/experim...` URL and receive HTTP 404.
- The generated bundle is `mitzvah-world.compact.js`; its behavior must be traced back to source and the CompactJS builder.
- Tunnel is connected to `Yackovs-MacBook-Air.local`.

## Remaining Work

1. Read current handoff, root HTML, source tree, generated bundle metadata, and Git state.
2. Trace readiness registration and discover why six required systems never become playable.
3. Trace Chossid asset URL construction and verify the canonical asset on disk and over HTTP.
4. Trace dynamic import rewriting for experiment modules in source and generated output.
5. Inspect CompactJS configuration, path rewriter, module ordering, and build entry points.
6. Choose the smallest root-cause repair that fixes source and generated modes without masking failure.
7. Rewrite every touched file in full; preserve unrelated user work.
8. Run syntax, build, focused tests, server/API checks, and browser runtime verification.
9. Re-read every touched file and compare planned versus actual work.
10. Record verification evidence, residual risks, and exact continuation state.

## Completion Gate

The ledger may close only when the public page boots without fatal console errors, required systems report playable, Chossid hydration no longer 404s, dynamic imports resolve, CompactJS rebuilds deterministically, and touched files pass readback plus tests.
